question.problem:
Use the model below to calculate $\dfrac{5}{6} \div 4.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14133144/assets/d1c1c3842b04174137bfe8a938c70493493b2c9a0e74bee619d965446c9326a6.png)
question.worked_solution:
Since we need to divide by $\color{blue}4$, we split the whole into $\color{blue}4$ equal parts horizontally.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14133144/assets/24bffed596b77ba53d57e04ebb6baede437d40f825c03a794ae7689f11c3c250.png)

From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents $\dfrac{5}{24}$ of the whole.

Therefore,

$$
\dfrac{5}{6} \div 4 = \dfrac{5}{24} \, .
$$
